claims.claim: Story of the Door introduces the austere lawyer Mr. Utterson
claims.evidence: Opening chapter on Mr. Utterson, 'a lawyer... austere with himself'

claims.claim: Enfield is Utterson's kinsman and they take Sunday walks
claims.evidence: 'Mr. Richard Enfield, his distant kinsman... in their Sunday walks'

claims.claim: Enfield points out a sinister door
claims.evidence: the door in the by-street told in chapter 1 (Enfield's story)

claims.claim: A brutal man trampled a child
claims.evidence: 'the man trampled calmly over the child's body and left her screaming'

claims.claim: He then paid her family with a cheque from a respected man
claims.evidence: 'pay them in a cheque'; 'the person that drew the cheque is the very pink of the proprieties'; 'The cheque was genuine'

claims.claim: Jekyll's will leaves everything to Mr. Hyde, a small, loathsome man
claims.evidence: Hyde 'pale and dwarfish... something downright detestable'; will naming Edward Hyde
chapter 'The Carew Murder Case': 'Sir Danvers Carew'; broken stick

claims.claim: Dr. Lanyon dies after a shock
claims.evidence: 'I have had a shock,' he said, 'and I shall never recover'

claims.claim: Poole fears foul play; he and Utterson break in and find Hyde dead in Jekyll's clothes
claims.evidence: 'I think there's been foul play,' said Poole; 'clothes far too large for him, clothes of the doctor's bigness'; the face of Edward Hyde

claims.claim: Jekyll drank a drug that turned him into Hyde, lost control of the change, and ran out of the salt
claims.evidence: 'My provision of the salt... began to run low... I drank it and it was without efficacy'

claims.claim: Hyde's handwriting matches Jekyll's, making Utterson suspect forgery
claims.evidence: 'the two hands are in many points identical'; 'Henry Jekyll forge for a murderer!'

claims.claim: Characters: Poole Jekyll's butler; Lanyon Jekyll's old friend, a physician
claims.evidence: Poole the servant of Jekyll's household; Lanyon's narrative of Jekyll
